dedupe_keys.name: ine uruguay censos 2023 population households and dwellings weighted anonymised microdata with dwelling and household files geocoded to department section segment locality and municipality plus household tables on sanitation disposal heating energy and dwelling materials

description: Uruguay's Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE) released the 2023 Censuses of population, households and dwellings as weighted anonymised microdata in its ANDA catalogue and as household and population tables. The microdata hold dwelling and person files with geographic codes for department, census section and segment, locality, Montevideo neighbourhood and municipality, and household variables on sanitary service and disposal, kitchen, heating and equipment. The published tables count private households by sanitation disposal and by heating energy source for the country, Montevideo and the interior, split into urban and rural areas. Of 1,373,546 private households, 854,446 were on the public sewer network and 492,440 used a septic tank or cesspit; 436,241 heated mainly with electricity and 479,748 with firewood. Format and access: free XLSX tables and microdata download after accepting INE terms. Licence: free use under INE terms, without redistributing or selling the microdata and citing INE. Caveats: the weighted files cover people actually counted, with weights expanding to the estimated population, and the tables are national, not local. Simulation uses: sewer connection and electric heating demand by segment or municipality, and synthetic households for agent models. Related records: the Argentina 2022, Chile 2024 and Paraguay 2022 census housing records.

schema_summary: Dwelling file: address and dwelling ids, DEPARTAMENTO, SECCION, SEGMENTO, LOCALIDAD, REGION_4, AREA, BARRIO85, CCZ, MUNICIPIO_136, dwelling type and occupancy. Household variable groups: tenure, rooms, sanitary service and its disposal, kitchen, heating, comfort and equipment, household members. Person file: demographics, migration, education, work. Tables: counts of private households by sanitation disposal (public network, septic tank, piped to stream, other, none) and by heating source (electricity, firewood, gas and others)
